subject: FlowOps + Redwood: lightweight plugin for prompt instrumentation & cache events
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex@promptsmith.ai>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
Cc: FlowOps Partnerships <partnerships@flowops.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Nov 2025 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: FlowOps x Redwood: plugin for prompt-level metrics + embedding cache events

Hi Maya —

Hope you’re well. I lead partnerships at PromptSmith and we work closely with FlowOps (cc’d) on orchestration + observability for prompt pipelines. FlowOps is shipping a lightweight integration they’re calling the "flowops-plugin" that can plug into LangChain callbacks and LlamaIndex event hooks to emit: token counts, prompt latencies, policy/temperature metadata, and embedding cache hit/miss events.

We think Redwood’s telemetry and caching model would be a great target for the plugin: it would allow ISVs and consultancies to (a) surface prompt-level metrics in Redwood Console, (b) correlate prompts <-> model variants served, and (c) drive smarter caching decisions (LRU hits, cross-request cache keys). FlowOps would like to pilot this with Redwood for a proof-of-concept to validate the telemetry schema and the minimal auth surface.

Attached is a short proposal (flowops-integration-proposal.pdf) that outlines two integration patterns and a suggested 4-week pilot. High level asks:
- Does Redwood support an ingestion endpoint for external prompt traces (signed, per-customer API key)?
- Best way to map FlowOps events to Redwood token/billing metadata?
- Any constraints on sending embedding cache events (hashes only, no raw vectors)?

We’re aiming for a quick discovery call this week to go over the tech pattern and pilot gating criteria. Would you and a couple folks from the Platform/Partner team be available?

Thanks — happy to adjust scope.

Best,
Alex Rivera
Head of Partnerships, PromptSmith
On behalf of FlowOps

Attachments: flowops-integration-proposal.pdf

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@promptsmith.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Nov 2025 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FlowOps x Redwood: plugin for prompt-level metrics + embedding cache events

Alex —

Thanks for the intro and the concise proposal — appreciate the clear asks. High level, we’re interested. A few quick clarifying points before we set a call:

- Deployment target: do you expect to integrate with Redwood Hosted API or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem)? You noted a pilot with per-customer API keys; for anything that emits trace-level data we generally recommend Private or a dedicated ingestion path.
- Data sensitivity: we can accept hash-only cache events (no raw vectors) — that aligns with our security patterns. We will need FlowOps to complete our security questionnaire and provide SOC2 A3 evidence.
- Telemetry mapping: token/billing metadata is typically derived from model response headers in our runtime; we can surface an ingestion endpoint for trace events but need a stable schema (we prefer JSON-LD-ish shape).

Cc’ing Marissa (partner ops) for commercial/go-to-market alignment and Ben (ecosystem cert) for any SDK/certification work. Karthik, can you join the discovery — want you to advise on the quickest integration pattern (sidecar vs SDK hook).

If next steps work, propose a 45-minute discovery Wednesday 11/05 10:00-10:45 PST. Please share any technical appendices (SDK samples, auth flow) beforehand.

Thanks,
Maya Srinivasan
Head of Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Evan Chu <evan@flowops.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>, Alex Rivera <alex@promptsmith.ai>
Date: Wed, 05 Nov 2025 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: FlowOps x Redwood: plugin for prompt-level metrics + embedding cache events

Hi Maya / Alex —

Quick intro — I’m the FlowOps engineer working on the plugin. Thanks for the fast turnaround, Maya. We prefer to run the plugin as an opt-in SDK extension (LangChain callbacks / LlamaIndex hooks) because that minimizes infra changes for our customers, but we have an alternate sidecar pattern if customers want middle-tier capture (e.g., legacy hosts). The attached technical notes (flowops-technical-patterns.md) describe both patterns and expected payloads.

Technical highlights:
- Auth: per-tenant API key with short TTL; payloads signed (HMAC-SHA256) and include a request_id to dedupe.
- Payload shape: event_type, timestamp, model_name, token_count, latency_ms, prompt_id, customer_id_hash, cache_event: {key_hash, hit_boolean}. No raw texts or vectors in the default mode.
- Volume expectations: during pilot we expect ~50-200 events/min for a mid-sized customer; supports gzip compression.
- LangChain/LlamaIndex integration: both expose callback/event hooks where we can emit the events with <50ms overhead per call (benchmarked).

Pilot asks from our side:
1) A staging ingestion endpoint and one Redwood Private sandbox account (or a test token) so we can exercise the HMAC auth and sample payloads.
2) A short SSO/integration checklist so Ben can do the certing work.
3) Agreement on retention: FlowOps will keep events for 30 days by default; Redwood should confirm retention/post-processing rules.

We can join Wed 11/05 at 10:00 PST — Alex will share a calendar invite. Let us know if you prefer a technical pre-read call first.

Thanks,
Evan Chu
Software Engineer, FlowOps

Attachments: flowops-technical-patterns.md
